chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan and Fadalah from Rifa'ah ibn Musa, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a Mutamatti' (one who performs Hajj al-Tamattu') who cannot find a sacrificial animal. He said: 'He should fast one day before Tarwiyah, the day of Tarwiyah, and the day of Arafah.'
I said: 'But he arrived on the day of Tarwiyah and then went out to Arafat.' He said: 'He should fast the three days after the departure (from Mina).'
I said: 'But his camel did not stay with him (i.e., he did not bring his sacrificial animal with him).' He said: 'He should fast the day of Husbah and two days after it.'
I said: 'Does he fast while he is a traveler?' He said: 'Yes, is he not a traveler on the day of Arafah?'
And Allah, the Exalted, says: 'Three days in Hajj.'
I said: 'Is the saying of Allah referring to Dhu al-Hijjah?'
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'And we, the People of the House, say it refers to Dhu al-Hijjah.'

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.التَّرْوِيَةِ: The 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah, when pilgrims proceed to Mina
key_terms.عَرَفَةَ: The 9th of Dhu al-Hijjah, the day of standing at Arafat
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٍ: A pilgrim who performs Umrah first, then Hajj, in the same season

ai.seo_question: What are the specific days of fasting for a Mutamatti' pilgrim who cannot afford a sacrificial animal?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific compensatory fasting schedule for a Mutamatti' pilgrim unable to afford a sacrificial animal, with the Imam adjusting the timing based on the pilgrim's travel status and animal presence. Imam al-Sadiq explicitly links this ruling to the Quranic phrase 'three days in Hajj,' asserting that the Ahl al-Bayt's interpretation of this verse confirms the obligation of fasting in Dhu al-Hijjah, thereby reinforcing the Shia jurisprudential stance on Hajj expiation.
